dedupe_keys.name: urbhealth abm agent based model of activity mobility air pollution and exposure under urban scenarios

description: UrbHealth-ABM is an agent-based model that simulates individual activity schedules and mobility choices, the traffic and NO2 air pollution they produce, and each person's exposure to pollution and transport-related physical activity under different urban scenarios. It was developed by Tabea Sonnenschein of Utrecht University for the paper 'Discovering environmental health effects of transport scenarios through agent-based simulations' in Environment International; version 1.0.1 with input data was archived on Zenodo on 16 October 2025. Built on Mesa, it routes walking, cycling, driving and transit trips with OSRM, assigns hourly traffic to a grid, computes NO2 with a hybrid dispersion model using cellular automata and built-environment moderators, and separates indoor and outdoor exposure; scenarios include no-emission zones, 15-minute city and higher parking fees. Coverage: the Amsterdam region, adaptable to other cities with similar data. Access: GitHub and Zenodo. Licence: GNU GPL 3.0; free. Caveats: needs substantial input data preparation and computing for large agent sets. Simulation uses: health impacts of transport and land-use interventions in streets and public spaces. Related records: the indoorContact ABM and JuPedSim.
